items.title: [Bug]: --otlp-traces-endpoint initializes tracer but never sends spans (instrument_otel/manual_instrument_otel never invoked)
items.body:
### Your current environment

### current environment

vLLM version: 0.29.0 (official `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` image)
Also reproduced on a custom fork/dev build (version reports as `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`)
Deployment: Kubernetes, single GPU (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) and 8x GPU tensor-parallel (custom GLM5Next model)
opentelemetry-sdk: 1.41.0 / 1.40.0 (confirmed on both builds)
opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http: matching versions
opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai: 0.5.1 (confirmed present)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When starting vLLM with `--otlp-traces-endpoint` (and optionally `--collect-detailed-traces`), the server starts successfully, serves real inference requests correctly, and vLLM's Prometheus metrics (`vllm:request_prefill_time_seconds`, `vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds`, etc.) show real per-request timing data. However, **no span data is ever transmitted to the configured OTLP endpoint**, confirmed via:

1. Zero matching log entries on the OTel Collector receiving end, across multiple test requests.
2. Zero movement in the collector's `otelcol_receiver_accepted_spans` Prometheus counter attributable to test traffic.
3. No trace-related log output anywhere in vLLM's own stdout/stderr, even with `--collect-detailed-traces all`.

This was reproduced identically on two independent vLLM builds — the official 0.29.0 release and an unrelated custom fork — ruling out a build-specific issue.

**Root cause, isolated via source inspection and runtime process inspection:**

- `instrument_otel()` and `manual_instrument_otel()` in `vllm/tracing/otel.py` are the only functions in the codebase capable of creating a populated span. A codebase-wide search shows **neither is called anywhere outside `vllm/tracing/otel.py` and `vllm/tracing/__init__.py` themselves**:


grep -rln '@instrument_otel|instrument_otel(|manual_instrument_otel' vllm/
→ only vllm/tracing/otel.py, vllm/tracing/init.py

- However, the tracer/exporter **does** get initialized somewhere in the `EngineCore` worker process — confirmed via runtime inspection (`/proc/<EngineCore-pid>/environ` contains `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`, which is only ever set programmatically by `init_otel_tracer()`), and `EngineCore` holds a real, `ESTABLISHED` TCP connection to the configured collector endpoint throughout the process lifetime.
- So the exporter object and its network connection are built correctly, but **nothing in the request-serving or engine-loop code path ever calls the span-creation functions to actually put data on that connection.**

This appears consistent with (but more specific than) #9952, which reports very limited/incomplete span coverage — in our case, coverage appears to be effectively zero for real request tracing.




One thing worth doing before submitting: search the existing issues for anything more recent than #9952 that might already cover this exact symptom — vLLM's tracing code may have changed since that report, and a maintainer will appreciate you noting "I searched and didn't find an exact duplicate" in the issue body if that's genuinely the case.



### 🐛 Describe the bug

## 📋 How to reproduce

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
  --otlp-traces-endpoint=http://<your-otel-collector>:4318/v1/traces \
  --collect-detailed-traces all
```

Send a real request:
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], "max_tokens": 10}'
```
Check the collector for any received span — none arrives, despite:
```bash
python3 -c "from vllm.tracing.otel import is_otel_available; print(is_otel_available())"
# → True
```

### ✔️ What I expected

A span for the request to appear at the configured OTLP endpoint, matching the documented behavior of `--otlp-traces-endpoint`.

### ❌ What actually happens

No span data is ever sent, with no error or warning logged anywhere, on any build tested.

### Additional notes

- Ruled out: missing `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai` (present, confirmed via `importlib.metadata`).
- Ruled out: gRPC-vs-HTTP protocol mismatch — `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf` was explicitly set in every test, and manual `curl` against the same endpoint confirms clean HTTP semantics end-to-end.
- Ruled out: network/TLS/collector misconfiguration — independently verified working via a separate, unrelated service (LiteLLM) successfully sending millions of spans to the same collector.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### 🐛 Describe the bug Since #54042 (`fdbf2ddbd2`) changed `CPUAttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` from `[MultipleOf(16)]` to `[MultipleOf(32)]` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/cpu_attn.py:61`), **81 tests under `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/` fail during worker construction on CPU-only machines**: ``` ValueError: No common block size for 16. ``` Representative traceback (`pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py -x --tb=short`): ``` tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py:229: in test_build_transfer_params_multi_group_trimming connector = MooncakeConnector( vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py:502: in __init__ self.connector_worker = MooncakeConnectorWorker( vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py:1046: in __init__ self._sync_block_size_with_kernel() vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py:1085: in _sync_block_size_with_kernel kernel_block_size = select_common_block_size(self.block_size, backends) vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:386: in select_common_block_size raise ValueError(f"No common block size for {kv_manager_block_size}.") E ValueError: No common block size for 16. ``` **Why CI doesn't see it.** These 81 tests are not marked `cpu_test`, so `misc.yaml` runs them only on the GPU lane (`-m 'not cpu_test'`), where the CPU attention backend is never selected. The 379 `cpu_test`-marked tests in the same directory have zero failures. #54042 did update the one `cpu_test`-marked file that CI flagged (`test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py`, 16 → 32) plus `tests/conftest.py`; the GPU-lane siblings were invisible to it. **Why it matters.** The connector unit tests are all-mock (fake backends, `MagicMock` workers, no kernels) and are the only part of the KV-connector suite a contributor without a GPU can run. Losing them locally means GPU-less contributors can no longer validate connector changes before pushing (I hit this while working on #55097). **Where it fails.** The connector worker's own kernel-block-size check at construction time: - `NixlKVConnectorBaseWorker._sync_block_size_with_kernel` (`kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py:794`) - `MooncakeConnectorWorker._sync_block_size_with_kernel` (`kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py:1079`) Both call `select_common_block_size(16, [CPUAttentionBackend])` → `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:386` raises. **Reproduce** (any CPU-only machine, `main` @ `7ee8a6dd01`): ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit -q -rf -p no:cacheprovider 2>&1 | tee before.log | tail -1 # 91 failed, 1437 passed, 27 skipped grep -c '^E .*No common block size for 16' before.log # 81 ``` The other 10 failures are pre-existing and unrelated (`test_hf3fs_connector` ×4, `test_multi_connector` ×1, `test_nixl_connector::test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller` ×2, `test_nixl_connector_hma::test_fewer_blocks_with_hma` ×1, `test_offloading_connector` ×2). ### Fix options — asking which shape you'd accept I read #54042 in full and take the 16 → 32 tightening as intentional (ISA is now computed per kv-cache group via `_set_isa_to_layers`, and `MultipleOf(32)` keeps every group on an optimized kernel rather than `vec16`). So I'm **not** proposing to revert the backend. The fix belongs on the test side, but the test suite has **two independent sources** of `block_size`, which shapes the options: 1. `create_vllm_config(block_size=16)` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py` → `cache_config.block_size` 2. `make_kv_cache_config(block_size=16)` / literal `FullAttentionSpec(block_size=16, ...)` → the worker's `self.block_size` is the lcm of the group specs (`base_worker.py:437`), and `cache_config.block_size` is only the fallback when there are no transfer groups. | Option | Change | Measured result | Trade-off | |---|---|---|---| | **(a)** Make `create_vllm_config` default platform-aware (`32 if is_cpu() else 16`), mirroring `tests/conftest.py::_default_block_size()` from #54042 | 1 line in `utils.py` | 103 → 86 failed: **+33 fixed, −16 newly broken** (source 2 still says 16, now mismatched with source 1) | Completing it means editing literal `16`s across ~23 files, some of which assert on tokens-per-block. Disproportionate. | | **(b)** New `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/conftest.py` with an autouse fixture that, on CPU only, monkeypatches `CPUAttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` → `[MultipleOf(16)]` | 1 new file, no test edits, no-op on GPU | **91 → 18 failed, `No common block size` 81 → 0, no test that passed before fails after** (remaining 8 are HF 429 rate-limit noise from back-to-back runs) | Reads as "the tests override what the backend declares". Justification: the connector worker only *consumes* the backend's declarations (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` for physical block size, `get_name()` for handshake metadata) and never executes its attention kernel, so the 32-multiple requirement — there to keep CPU attention on optimized ISA paths — has no bearing on the connector logic under test; with the mock, `select_common_block_size(16, ...)` returns 16 and the tests run exactly as they did before #54042. Precedent: 6 tests in this directory already stub `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` on a fake backend (`test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`); the conftest lifts that to a directory default. | | **(c)** `create_vllm_config(block_size=None)` and let the platform choose | 1 line | not measured | On the GPU lane Phase 1 selection would pick the backend's preferred size, which may differ from 16 → changes GPU-lane behavior; still has the two-sources problem. | I have (b) implemented and verified locally and can open a PR immediately; happy to do (a) properly instead if the CPU or connector owners prefer the tests to genuinely use 32 on CPU. **Side observation**, not part of the ask: `platforms/cpu.py:273` only *warns* "CPU backend prefers block_size is multiples of 32" and lets 16 through, whereas the same function force-overrides `block_size` for MLA/DSv4. The eventual error (`No common block size for 16.`) doesn't name the backend or the constraint that rejected it. cc @bigPYJ1151 (author of #54042) --- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for investigation and drafting; I reviewed every claim and ran every command above myself. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: vllm bench serve may overcount peak concurrent requests at integer-second boundaries
items.body:
### Your current environment

- OS: Linux container; two-node deployment (private host details omitted)
- Python: 3.12.13
- vLLM runtime: 0.28.0+cu129
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu129 (CUDA 12.9)
- Ray: 2.48.0
- Model: Kimi K3
- Source inspection: vLLM main snapshot d86257e (2026-09-12)

The benchmark output and logs are available on request; no private host addresses, credentials, or raw service logs are included here.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Description

`vllm bench serve` currently computes `max_concurrent_requests` by mapping each request to integer-second buckets and incrementing every bucket from `int(start)` through `int(end)`, inclusive. For adjacent half-open intervals that only touch at a boundary, this can report two concurrent requests even though exact instantaneous concurrency is one.

This is a benchmark-metric issue, not evidence that the serving engine accepts more requests than `--max-concurrency`.

### Minimal reproduction

The following CPU-only witness mirrors the current bucket loop:

```python
def bucket_peak(intervals):
    buckets = [0, 0, 0]
    for start, end in intervals:
        for second in range(int(start), int(end) + 1):
            buckets[second] += 1
    return max(buckets), buckets

def exact_peak(intervals):
    events = sorted((t, delta) for start, end in intervals
                    for t, delta in ((start, 1), (end, -1)))
    active = peak = 0
    for _, delta in events:
        active += delta
        peak = max(peak, active)
    return peak

intervals = [(0.0, 1.0), (1.0, 2.0)]
print("current_bucket_peak=", bucket_peak(intervals))
print("exact_sweep_peak=", exact_peak(intervals))
```

Observed output:

```text
current_bucket_peak=(2, [1, 2, 1])
exact_sweep_peak=1
```

### Real benchmark observation

The two-node benchmark used vLLM 0.28.0+cu129, Kimi K3, 1024 random input tokens, 128 forced output tokens, one warmup, request rate `inf`, and completed requests without failures:

| Configured max_concurrency | Reported max_concurrent_requests |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 4 |
| 4 | 8 |
| 8 | 16 |
| 16 | 32 |

This is an observation of the benchmark JSON field; it is not a claim that server-side admission exceeded the configured limit.

### Source observation

In the current main `vllm/benchmarks/serve.py` `calculate_metrics()` path, the relevant logic is equivalent to:

```python
request_start_second = int(output.start_time - min_start_time)
request_end_second = int(output.start_time + output.latency - min_start_time)
for second in range(request_start_second, request_end_second + 1):
    concurrent_requests_per_second[second] += 1
```

The local source snapshot was commit `d86257e`. The inclusive `+ 1` needs confirmation against the intended metric contract.

### Related issue

[vLLM #37666](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37666) is related because it also discusses `vllm bench serve` metrics and shows a peak-concurrency value above the configured maximum. However, that report centers on output-throughput inconsistency and does not isolate this inclusive bucket-boundary behavior.

### Question

Is inclusive one-second bucket occupancy intentional for `max_concurrent_requests`, or should this field represent exact instantaneous concurrency? If the latter, I can prepare a small CPU-only regression test and a minimal fix.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Examples from generic test prompts (no system prompt, no sampling parameters from the client): - *Travel保险 Tips: wear comfortable shoes and carry water* - **From情节 to Spoiler — Quick Summary** - he and hisгляur close friend **Mr. Darcy** become acquainted - The \PD Treaty of common边 issues is 语言 — translation: when in dough that you doubt proof. 佛.` (22 CJK characters in a sourdough answer) ## Repro ### Serving config ```sh vllm serve s3:///glm-5.3-flash/ \ # Or any local dir would also work I guess for this purpose --load-format runai_streamer \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"distributed": true, "concurrency": 16}' \ --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --trust-remote-code \ --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager --enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' # env: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 RUNAI_STREAMER_S3_TARGET_GBPS=1 RUNAI_STREAMER_S3_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=30000 RUNAI_STREAMER_DIST_TIMEOUT=60 ``` ### Test script ```py import re, json, urllib.request FOREIGN = re.compile(r'[一-鿿㐀-䶿぀-ヿ가-힯Ѐ-ӿ฀-๿؀-ۿऀ-ॿ֐-׿]') prompts = ["Explain what a Kubernetes StatefulSet is and when to use one instead of a Deployment.", "Give me a 3-day Lisbon itinerary with one highlight per day.", "Summarize the plot of Pride and Prejudice in five sentences.", "My sourdough loaves come out dense. Three likely causes and fixes?"] # etc., ~12 varied prompts for p in prompts: body = {"model": "zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": p}], "max_tokens": 1200} r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request("http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})) content = json.loads(r.read())["choices"][0]["message"].get("content") or "" print(len(FOREIGN.findall(content)), content[:120].replace("\n", " ")) ``` ## Potential Root Cause I looked into the code around the weight streamer for this model, and here's what I can tell, pls correct me if I'm not looking in the right direction: 1. When streaming, I see that the pending pair is created per call of `load_weights()`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9d88ceb02694c6e3df182ec3c87201284f50e2c6/vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py#L758-L795 2. When `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj` is called and if `weights` or `scale` aren't in the entry, it doesn't mark anything as loaded and returns `True` (this is expected IIUC): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9d88ceb02694c6e3df182ec3c87201284f50e2c6/vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py#L1230-L1255 3. `AutoWeightsLoader` ultimately calls `load_weights()` which returns once it comes across vision tensors eventhough the next group would have had a matching second half for (2) https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9d88ceb02694c6e3df182ec3c87201284f50e2c6/vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py#L247-L265 4. The reason this shows up with `distributed` mode is that with run:ai model streamer v0.16.1 (the latest), it [partitions the files by `chunks` ](https://github.com/dsx-ai-factory/runai-model-streamer/blob/7093b77482db55146d2665e6fd4cfbec0b4fe99c/py/runai_model_streamer/runai_model_streamer/distributed_streamer/partition.py#L26) and round-robins the chunks it assigns to ranks. Therefore, a `.weight` and its corresponding `_scale_inv` can end up on different ranks with a vision tensor file in between them, and when processed by a rank in order, can lead to the behaviour described above. ### Note Run:ai model streamer changed the default parition policy on `master` which might alleviate this issue for GLM 5.3 Flash, and consequently setting `RUNAI_STREAMER_PARTITION_POLICY=files` leads to the same issue too. It is worth noting that `spans` (only on `master` and not in 0.16.1) provides no such guarantee that the above descirbed sequence cannot occur since its just a different way of splitting and assigning the checkpoint layout. ## Prior Art - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46078 - same issue for a DeepSeek model - https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash/discussions/23 - bug report with distributed streaming - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38991 (talks about a similar symptom but not in `distributed` mode) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### Your current environment

    - Model: `GLM-5.3-Flash` 
    
    Full launch command:
    
    ```bash
    vllm serve \
      --model GLM-5.3-Flash \
      --enable-prefix-caching \
      --performance-mode interactivity \
      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --served-model-name glm \
      --enable-expert-parallel \
      --port 8001 --host 0.0.0.0 \
      --max-model-len 524288 \
      --tool-call-parser glm47 \
      --reasoning-parser glm45 \
      --enable-auto-tool-choice \
      --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
      --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
      --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 20 \
      --mm-processor-kwargs '{"min_pixels": 313600, "max_pixels": 2073600}' \
      --limit-mm-per-prompt.videos 0 \
      --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
      --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'

Notes:

* We also tried **vLLM 0.29.0**, but the server fails to start with this configuration.

* The failure below is **independent** of the parsers / speculative config / vision options, because it also reproduces on **`/tokenize`**, which does not touch any of them (see "Isolation" below).

* * *

### 🐛 Describe the bug

For a specific class of input strings, the API server **closes the TCP connection without sending any HTTP response at all** (zero response bytes — no status line, no headers, no body). The client therefore observes a bare connection error rather than an HTTP error.

This is not a transient/flaky issue: it reproduces **deterministically, 100% of the time**, and it is **content-dependent** — changing one character (or removing a single trailing slash) makes it disappear.

**Impact in production:** our agent workload sends full conversations back to the model on every step. Once a conversation contains an assistant message with a matching substring (e.g. a file path such as `2023/2024/2025.md` preceded by the word "and"), **every subsequent request in that conversation fails**. With client-side retries this manifests as repeated `APIConnectionError: Connection error.` with **zero output tokens**, and the engine never sees the request (no `abort`, no `error`, nothing in `/metrics`). Roughly **40–60% of agent sessions** eventually became stuck this way.

* * *

### 🐍 Minimal reproduction

The crash is reachable **without any chat template, engine, scheduler, tool parser or speculative decoding involved** — simply by calling `/tokenize`:

    curl -sS -X POST http://<HOST>:<PORT>/tokenize \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model":"glm-chat","prompt":"and 2023/"}'
    # => curl: (52) Empty reply from server
    #    client receives ZERO response bytes

The identical request **without the trailing slash** works fine:

    curl -sS -X POST http://<HOST>:<PORT>/tokenize \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model":"glm-chat","prompt":"and 2023"}'
    # => {"count":3,"max_model_len":524288,"tokens":[...]}

End-to-end repro through the normal chat path:

    curl -sS -X POST http://<HOST>:<PORT>/v1/chat/completions \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model":"glm-chat","stream":true,"max_completion_tokens":8,
           "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"and 2023/"}]}'
    # => curl: (52) Empty reply from server

* * *

### ✅ Expected behavior

The server should return an HTTP error response (e.g. `400`/`500` with a JSON error body), **or** tokenize successfully. It should **never** close the connection with zero response bytes.

### ❌ Actual behavior

TCP connection is closed by the server with **0 response bytes**. No status line, no headers, no body, no traceback surfaced to the client. The API server stays alive and continues serving other requests normally (subsequent healthy requests return `200`).

* * *

### 🔬 Control matrix (all on `/tokenize`, 2 runs each, 100% deterministic)

| prompt | result |
| --- | --- |
| `"hi"` | ✅ 200 |
| `"2023/"` | ✅ 200 |
| `"and"` | ✅ 200 |
| `"and 2023"` ← *no trailing `/`* | ✅ 200 |
| `"and2023/"` ← *no space after `and`* | ✅ 200 |
| `"the 2023/"` | ✅ 200 |
| `"an 2023/"` | ✅ 200 |
| `"and 2023/x"` ← *character after `/`* | ✅ 200 |
| **`"and 2023/"`** | ❌ **empty reply** |
| **`"and 1234/"`** | ❌ **empty reply** |
| **`"and 23/"`** | ❌ **empty reply** |
| **`"and 0000/"`** | ❌ **empty reply** |
| **`"AND 2023/"`** ← *case-insensitive* | ❌ **empty reply** |
| **`"and 2023/"`** ← *two spaces* | ❌ **empty reply** |
| **`"x and 2023/"`** | ❌ **empty reply** |
| **`"and 2023/ "`** | ❌ **empty reply** |
| **`"and 2023/2024/"`** | ❌ **empty reply** |

**Characterization of the trigger:** the tokenizer crashes for input matching

    <word ending in "and"> <whitespace>+ <digits> / (end-of-input | whitespace | /)

* the word `and` is required (`the`, `an`, a single letter do **not** trigger)
* whitespace between `and` and the digits is required
* a `/` immediately after the digits is required
* the `/` must be followed by end-of-string, whitespace, or another `/`; any other character after the `/` (`"and 2023/x"`) does **not** trigger

* * *

| observation | implication |
| --- | --- |
| Reproduces on **`POST /tokenize`** with a plain `prompt` | No chat template, no engine, no scheduler involved |
| Reproduces with `stream: false` and with no optional params | Not related to streaming or request options |
| Reproduces with `role: user` and with `role: assistant` | Not related to message roles |

Server-side logs around such a request would confirm; we unfortunately do not have access to them, which is why we are reporting it here.

    output tokens: 0
    retries: 5/5 failed with the identical body

Because the API server closes the connection at the TCP level, the client cannot distinguish this from a network failure, which made this bug very hard to localize before we captured the exact request body and reduced it to the repro above.

Happy to provide the full original request body (171 KB, 39 messages, 40 tools) if useful, but the 5-character reproduction above should be sufficient.

items.title: [Bug]: Unconditional xgrammar import in backend_xgrammar.py crashes vLLM startup on s390x
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Platform: s390x (IBM Z / LinuxONE) vLLM version: 0.28.0 Python: 3.11 OS: RHEL / UBI 9 (s390x) GPU / accel: IBM Spyre (custom accelerator, not CUDA) xgrammar: not installed — no pre-built wheel available for s390x; apache-tvm-ffi (build dependency) also has no s390x support ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug On `s390x` (IBM Z / LinuxONE), vLLM 0.28.0 crashes at startup with an `ImportError` before serving any requests. The crash originates in `vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py`, which imports `xgrammar` unconditionally at class-definition time. `xgrammar` has no pre-built wheels for `s390x` and cannot be built from source on the platform because it requires `apache-tvm-ffi`, which also has no `s390x` support. Because the import is unconditional and happens at module load, there is no way to use vLLM on `s390x` at all — including for workloads that never use structured output — without providing a stub module as a workaround. **Affected file**: `vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py` ```python from vllm import LLM # crashes here — never reaches model load llm = LLM(model="facebook/opt-125m") ``` ``` ImportError: No module named 'xgrammar' File "vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py", line N, in import xgrammar as xgr ``` **Proposed fix**: Wrap the import in a `try/except ImportError` guard, consistent with how other optional platform backends are handled throughout vLLM: ```python try: import xgrammar as xgr HAS_XGRAMMAR = True except ImportError: xgr = None HAS_XGRAMMAR = False ``` Then raise a clear `RuntimeError("xgrammar is not available on this platform")` only if a user actually requests the xgrammar structured-output backend. **Current workaround**: Install a minimal Python stub package for `xgrammar` with a valid `__file__` attribute to satisfy the import. **Related**: #9652 — "[RFC]: Add support for IBM Spyre accelerator" — prior context for IBM Z / s390x vLLM support. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug # [Bug] extract_hidden_states uses first-column feedback for multi-token outputs ## Summary When using `extract_hidden_states` with async scheduling, I observed reproducible duplicated digits and punctuation in generated answers. I traced this to `ExtractHiddenStatesProposer.prepare_next_token_ids_padded()`: it reads only column 0 of `sampled_token_ids`, although a decoding iteration can produce two valid sampled tokens with `num_speculative_tokens=1`. For a non-discarded row `[15, 18]`, the original helper returns: ~~~text actual: valid_count=1, next_token_id=15 expected: valid_count=2, next_token_id=18 ~~~ Both tokens can already be included in the valid output sent to the scheduler. The helper therefore reports different progress and a different continuation token from the committed output. A local fix that reuses `eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel` restored the exact healthy baseline token IDs on three document samples, including a four-request sequence with diagnostic tracing disabled. Hidden extraction remained enabled, and two-token output steps still occurred. ## Environment - **Installed vLLM version / wheel or commit:** TODO — paste the actual build identity below. - **Model:** NuExtract3, 4B multimodal checkpoint. **Exact model repository and revision:** TODO. - **Hardware / driver / CUDA / PyTorch:** TODO — include collect_env output. - **Tensor parallelism:** 1. - **Relevant source:** the first-column implementation is present in the [v0.26.0 Hidden proposer source](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.26.0/api/vllm/v1/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states/). This source reference is separate from the installed-build information requested above. - No third-party `vllm-hook` plugin was loaded in the tested NuExtract3 environment. Relevant configuration: | Setting | Value | |---|---| | `max_model_len` | 65536 | | `max_num_batched_tokens` | 65536 | | `max_num_seqs` | 1 | | `gpu_memory_utilization` | 0.88 | | dtype | bfloat16 | | Chunked prefill / prefix caching | Both disabled | | Async scheduling | Enabled in the observed runtime | | CUDA Graph | Default; also tested with `--enforce-eager` | | Native `qwen3_next_mtp` | Disabled | | Request sampling | temperature=0.2, seed=0, thinking disabled | | Request output limit | 16384; the core short reproductions did not reach it | | Client logprobs / prompt_logprobs | Not requested | | HTTP token IDs | Requested and saved directly | | Hidden export | Same-request prompt + decode, `include_output_tokens=true` | Speculative configuration: ~~~json { "method": "extract_hidden_states", "num_speculative_tokens": 1, "draft_model_config": { "hf_config": { "eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids": [32] } } } ~~~ The connector was `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`, with `kv_role=kv_producer`, synchronization locking enabled, and eight writer threads.
Environment output Run this in the serving environment: ~~~bash python -m vllm.collect_env ~~~ ~~~text TODO: paste the actual collect_env output here. ~~~
## Minimal helper-level reproducer The installed function was tested directly with small CUDA tensors; in particular, `[15, 18]` produced `count=1,next=15` before the fix and `count=2,next=18` after it. Below is a reduced harness for that interface. It calls the actual installed helper, without constructing a model or running the scheduler. Only the backup buffer and request metadata are lightweight stand-ins. **Execution status of this newly packaged harness:** TODO — run it in the affected serving environment and replace this note with the actual output before submitting. The end-to-end results below come from the completed investigation, not from an execution of this newly packaged script. Save as `repro_hidden_feedback.py`, then run: ~~~bash python repro_hidden_feedback.py ~~~ ~~~python import hashlib import inspect import json import sys from types import SimpleNamespace import torch import vllm from vllm.v1.spec_decode.extract_hidden_states import ( ExtractHiddenStatesProposer, ) if not torch.cuda.is_available(): raise SystemExit("This reproducer requires a CUDA-capable vLLM environment.") device = torch.device("cuda") backup_token = 42 class BackupBuffer: """Only the buffer interface used by the real helper is needed.""" def __init__(self, size): self.host = torch.empty(size, dtype=torch.int32, device="cpu") self.np = self.host.numpy() self.gpu = torch.empty(size, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) def copy_to_gpu(self, size): self.gpu[:size].copy_(self.host[:size]) rows = [ [15, -1], # one valid output in two slots [15, 18], # two different valid outputs [15, 15], # two identical valid outputs [0, -1], # token ID 0 is valid [-1, -1], # no valid output: use backup [15, 18], # discarded request: count 0 and use backup ] discard_flags = [False, False, False, False, False, True] size = len(rows) request_ids = [f"request-{i}" for i in range(size)] fake_proposer = SimpleNamespace(backup_next_token_ids=BackupBuffer(size)) batch = SimpleNamespace( num_reqs=size, req_ids=request_ids, num_tokens_no_spec=[1] * size, vocab_size=256, ) requests = { request_id: SimpleNamespace(get_token_id=lambda position: backup_token) for request_id in request_ids } sampled = torch.tensor(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) discard = torch.tensor(discard_flags, dtype=torch.bool, device=device) helper = ExtractHiddenStatesProposer.prepare_next_token_ids_padded source = inspect.getsource(helper) print(json.dumps({ "python": sys.executable, "vllm_version": vllm.__version__, "helper_module": inspect.getfile(helper), "helper_source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(source.encode()).hexdigest(), }, indent=2)) with torch.inference_mode(): next_ids, counts = helper( fake_proposer, sampled, requests, batch, discard ) # Synchronization here is intentional: this is a standalone function test, # not a hook inserted into a running generation loop. observed = { "valid_counts": counts.cpu().tolist(), "next_ids": next_ids.cpu().tolist(), } expected = { "valid_counts": [1, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0], "next_ids": [15, 18, 15, 0, backup_token, backup_token], } print(json.dumps({"observed": observed, "expected": expected}, indent=2)) assert observed == expected, "Hidden feedback does not match valid sampled outputs" ~~~ For the linked first-column implementation, the values predicted by the code are: ~~~text valid_counts = [1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1] next_ids = [15, 15, 15, 0, 42, 42] ~~~ The two-valid-token rows expose the main issue. The discarded row also checks consistency with the existing EAGLE feedback contract. ## Expected behavior For each non-discarded request, the helper should: 1. Count all valid sampled output columns. 2. Return the last valid sampled token as the continuation token. 3. Return count 0 and a backup token when there are no valid sampled outputs. 4. Return count 0 and a backup token for a discarded request. Unused output slots are `-1`; token ID 0 is valid. `num_speculative_tokens=1` constrains the draft length. It does not imply that the rejection sampler can only return one valid output token: an accepted draft plus an additional target-model token can produce two outputs. ## Source-level findings The relevant function is: ~~~text vllm/v1/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states.py ExtractHiddenStatesProposer.prepare_next_token_ids_padded ~~~ The implementation selects: ~~~python sampled = sampled_token_ids[:, 0] ~~~ It computes the valid count from that single column and also selects the continuation token from that column. Its comment assumes a one-column sampled result because the speculative length is one. See the [official source](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.26.0/api/vllm/v1/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states/). By contrast, the [existing EAGLE feedback kernel](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.26.0/api/vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils/) counts all valid columns, selects the last valid token, and handles discard/backup cases. The [base proposer](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.26.0/api/vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer/) already uses it. The Hidden branch in [GPUModelRunner](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.26.0/api/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner/) passes the helper outputs to `_copy_valid_sampled_token_count()`. The count participates in subsequent async state corrections, and the continuation token is stored for subsequent input preparation. These are execution inputs, not just logging metadata. ## End-to-end observations With the same document, template, decoding parameters, and seed, enabling the Hidden path produced errors such as: | Field | Healthy baseline, Hidden off | Hidden on, before fix | |---|---|---| | Previous balance | `277.79` | `277..79` | | Previous reading | `40036` | `400336` | | Usage quantity | `669` | `6699` | The malformed output was already present in the original token ID sequence. It was not introduced by HTTP detokenization or JSON repair. For the short `we-energies-sample-bill` case: | Metric | Hidden off | Hidden on, before fix | Hidden on, after local fix | |---|---:|---:|---:| | HTTP output token count, including stop token | 326 | 332 | 326 | | Token IDs equal to Hidden-off baseline | — | No | Yes, every ID | | ExtractBench Value F1 | 1.0 | 0.5238 | 1.0 | | Strict JSON | Yes | No | Yes | | Hidden export | Not requested | Successful | Successful | The first differing output ID was at zero-based index 29, in the account number, before the later malformed decimal. Commit-side tracing showed that every formal append matched the valid output received by the scheduler. Concatenating those appends exactly reconstructed the final HTTP sequence: | Run | One-token appends | Two-token appends | Total append calls | Total output tokens | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Before fix | 320 | 6 | 326 | 332 | | After fix | 314 | 6 | 320 | 326 | Thus, the fix did **not** work by suppressing two-token outputs or deleting repeated tokens after generation. After removing the diagnostic hooks, this request sequence also passed: | Request order | Document | Patched output | |---:|---|---| | 1 | we-energies | 326 IDs, exactly equal to baseline and the traced fixed run; strict JSON | | 2 | ti_spec | 1301 IDs, exactly equal to baseline; strict JSON | | 3 | hingham | 487 IDs, exactly equal to baseline; Value F1=0.8846, its healthy baseline | | 4 | we-energies again | Same IDs as request 1 and baseline; Value F1=1.0 | Hidden remained enabled. For the fixed we-energies run, the exported completion IDs matched the HTTP output IDs except for the final sampled token; the same-request export succeeded. Vector-by-vector numerical validation is separate and not claimed here. The end-to-end data require the original document and extraction template. The helper reproducer above isolates the feedback contract without those inputs. ## Controls already tested - The failure occurs on the first business request after a fresh restart. - Independent restarts reproduced the same bad we-energies token sequence. - Turning off native MTP without enabling Hidden did not reproduce the degradation. - Requesting logprobs without Hidden did not reproduce it; the failing Hidden runs did not request logprobs. - The Hidden-off control used the same 65536 window and disabled chunked prefill/prefix caching. - Default and `--enforce-eager` produced identical IDs within each Hidden-on/off group. - A separate default-mode bridge run at utilization 0.90 reproduced the same bad 332-ID sequence as utilization 0.88. - Observation-only tracing preserved the unpatched output IDs; the local fix remained effective after those hooks were removed. ## Local fix and proposed regression coverage The only functional change for the fixed runs was to replace the Hidden helper's first-column logic with the existing `eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel`, preserving the existing backup-token preparation. The change returns both: - the full valid sampled-output count; - the last valid sampled token. It also follows the kernel's discard behavior. The `propose()` return slice `[:, :1]` was left unchanged, as were the sampler, scheduler append logic, connector, model weights, and request sampling parameters. Actual GPU function tests passed for two valid outputs, discarded requests, token ID 0, and mixed batches. The end-to-end evidence supports the **feedback-interface fix as a whole**; I have not separately isolated a count-only fix from a continuation-token-only fix. Suggested regression cases: - `[15, -1]` → count 1, next 15. - `[15, 18]` → count 2, next 18. - `[15, 15]` → count 2, next 15. - Token ID 0 remains valid. - No valid outputs → count 0, backup. - Discarded request → count 0, backup. - Mixed rows and repeated helper calls do not mix request state. Could the Hidden proposer reuse the existing feedback kernel, with these cases added as regression tests? ## Evidence boundaries and related work - Async CPU getter logs were not reliably aligned to GPU production iterations by a simple incrementing log ID. I do **not** claim a directly observed per-iteration GPU feedback value from those logs. The evidence is the real helper's behavior, the observed multi-token result shape/content, the caller's consumption of this interface, and the local-fix regression results. - Exact token-ID recovery is an observed result for these test cases, not a general claim that different speculative paths must share an identical seeded random-number trajectory. - The post-fix checks cover three distinct documents and a four-request sequence. Full-dataset post-fix regression and all-model/all-version coverage are not claimed. - This appears separate from [PR #38610](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38610). That fix addresses `propose()` returning the wrong draft shape, as described in the [official advisory](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-83vm-p52w-f9pw). This issue concerns the feedback helper consuming sampled outputs, and the local fix does not change the draft-return slice. - I have not established the complete affected-version range or confirmed whether current main contains a separate fix. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_raj-rarihar ### 🐛 Describe the bug

Summary

--cpu-offload-gb N consumes roughly 1.9N GiB of host memory rather than N, on Qwen/QwQ-32B-AWQ. The engine's own accounting reports N, so nothing visible contradicts the flag while the machine is holding almost twice it.

What I expected

--cpu-offload-gb 4 moves about 4 GiB of decoder-layer weights into host memory. Host memory attributable to the offload is about 4 GiB, and Total CPU offloaded parameters: 4.0 agrees with what the machine paid.

What happens

The weights move correctly and the model serves. But the engine process's resident shared memory reaches 8.01 GB for a 4 GiB (4.29 GB) request, a factor of 1.87. Total CPU offloaded parameters still reports the requested figure, because the offloader counts what it asked the allocator for rather than what the allocator handed back.


The factor is not constant. It depends on the tensor shapes, and vLLM's fused projections happen to land just above a power of two.

Why it matters

Offload is used precisely when memory is scarce, and this flag is the only control the operator has over it. Sizing a deployment from it under-provisions the host by the same factor. On a 32 GB box, asking for 12 GiB of offload wants roughly 24 GB, leaving too little for the rest of the machine; the failure mode is the OOM killer taking the engine during weight loading, with nothing in the log pointing at the offload.


It also makes the flag hard to tune, since lowering it to fit the host lowers the resident share by 1.9x more than intended, pushing weights back onto a device that was already short.

Root cause

UVAOffloader._maybe_offload_to_cpu pins each offloaded parameter:


cpu_data = p.data.to(device="cpu")


if self.pin_memory:


    cpu_data = cpu_data.pin_memory()


...


self.cpu_offload_bytes += p.data.numel() * p.data.element_size()


pin_memory() allocates through PyTorch's CachingHostAllocator, which rounds every request up to the next power of two:


const auto roundSize = [&]() -> size_t {


  if (size <= pinned_max_round_threshold() &&


      size <= pinned_max_cached_size()) {


    return c10::llvm::PowerOf2Ceil(size);


  } else {


    return size;


  }


}();


Both thresholds default to std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max() (c10/core/AllocatorConfig.h), so the rounding always applies, and freed blocks are cached rather than returned to the OS.


cpu_offload_bytes is charged the true tensor size, so the budget is spent at one rate while the host pays at another.

How big

Qwen/QwQ-32B-AWQ, one decoder layer at the fused shapes vLLM builds:


tensor | nominal | allocated | ratio -- | -- | -- | -- gate_up_proj.qweight | 141.56 MB | 268.44 MB | 1.90 down_proj.qweight | 70.78 MB | 134.22 MB | 1.90 qkv_proj.qweight | 18.35 MB | 33.55 MB | 1.83 o_proj.qweight | 13.11 MB | 16.78 MB | 1.28 one layer | 253.34 MB | 470.71 MB | 1.86

Other shapes fare better: Llama 3.3 70B AWQ comes out at 1.18 and an 8B fp16 at 1.15. Still 15% of a multi-gigabyte budget.

Reproduction

pin_overhead_probe.py (attached) allocates one layer's worth of tensors at those shapes both ways, one process per mode so the caching allocator starts empty each time. RTX 5070 Ti, vLLM 0.29.0:


  mode           asked for    resident shmem   ratio


  pinned         1013.4 MB         1891.6 MB    1.87


  mapped         1013.4 MB         1022.7 MB    1.01


pinned is Tensor.pin_memory(), what the offloader does today. mapped leaves the tensor unpinned, so get_cuda_view_from_cpu_tensor takes its other branch and does an exact cudaHostAlloc. 1.87 measured against 1.86 predicted from the shapes alone.


End to end, same box, offload_serve_probe.py (attached) running vllm serve Qwen/QwQ-32B-AWQ --cpu-offload-gb 4 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 32:


pin_memory on    asked 4.29 GB   engine RssShmem 8.01 GB   1.87x


pin_memory off   asked 4.29 GB   engine RssShmem 4.34 GB   1.01x


off via VLLM_WEIGHT_OFFLOADING_DISABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1. Both runs stop at the same point (4 GiB offloaded leaves ~15 GB of weights on a 16 GB card, so engine init runs out of device memory), so weight loading completes identically in both and the host figures are comparable. Total CPU offloaded parameters reports the same value either way.

Workaround

VLLM_WEIGHT_OFFLOADING_DISABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1.


Happy to open a PR if that is the direction you want.

items.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: SimpleCPUOffloadConnector crashes with `assert block_size % hash_block_size == 0` (block_size=8, hash_block_size=32)
items.body:
### Your current environment

## Environment

- Hardware: 8 × H100 80GB (HBM3), CUDA 13
- vLLM version: `0.1.dev20904+g179dd0fa9` (image `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909`)
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (fp8, hybrid KV cache: MLA full-attention group @ block_size 32 + SWA/circular-buffer group @ block_size 8; DSpark MTP speculative decoding)
- Python 3.12, TP=8, EP=8

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

Serving `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (hybrid KV: full-attention MLA + sliding-window/circular-buffer groups) with the `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` crashes the EngineCore on the **first scheduled request** with:

```
(EngineCore pid=536) [ASSERT-DEBUG] resolve_block_hashes: block_size=8, hash_block_size=32, modulo=8   <-- our instrumented print, see note below
(EngineCore pid=536) ERROR ... assert block_size % hash_block_size == 0
AssertionError
```

(The `[ASSERT-DEBUG]` line is **not** stock vLLM output — we volume-mounted a patched `kv_cache_utils.py` into the container that prints `block_size`/`hash_block_size`/modulo just before the assert, since the bare `AssertionError` carries no values. Stock vLLM produces only the assert line; details in *Extra context*.)

Note `block_size (8) < hash_block_size (32)` — the call asks `resolve_block_hashes` to view 32-token-granularity hashes at a *finer* 8-token granularity, but the function only supports the coarsening direction (`block_size >= hash_block_size`, enforced by the divisibility assert). With 8 < 32 the assert `8 % 32 == 0` can never hold, so the crash is deterministic on the first request.

## Deploy command (paths/ports/keys elided)

```bash
docker run --gpus all --privileged --ipc=host --net=host \
  <model-volume-mounts> \
  vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909 \
  vllm serve <model-path> \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80, 88, 96, 104, 112, 120, 128, 136, 144, 152, 160]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":118111600640,"lazy_offload":false}}'
```

Note on `--compilation-config`: the default cudagraph capture sizes (up to 512 with profiling) OOM on this model+hardware, so capture sizes are explicitly capped at 160.

## Reproduction

1. Start the server with the command above. Startup completes normally (weights load, CPU offload pool allocates, CUDA graphs capture, "Application startup complete").
2. Send any request that triggers KV offload bookkeeping (e.g. a chat completion with a long prompt).
3. EngineCore crashes immediately in the scheduler step:

```
(EngineCore pid=536) [ASSERT-DEBUG] resolve_block_hashes: block_size=8, hash_block_size=32, modulo=8
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1430, in run_busy_loop
    self._process_engine_step()
  File ".../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 1373, in schedule
    meta = self._build_kv_connector_meta(self.connector, scheduler_output)
  File ".../vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py", line 268, in build_connector_meta
    return self.scheduler_manager.build_connector_meta(scheduler_output)
  File ".../vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py", line 453, in build_connector_meta
    store_gpu, store_cpu, store_req_ids, store_meta = self.prepare_store_specs(...)
  File ".../vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py", line 523, in prepare_store_specs
    return self._prepare_eager_store_specs(scheduler_output)
  File ".../vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py", line 638, in _prepare_eager_store_specs
    self._select_eager_blocks_to_store(state, block_ids_by_group)
  File ".../vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py", line 720, in _select_eager_blocks_to_store
    resolved_hashes = resolve_block_hashes(
  File ".../vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py", line 2788, in resolve_block_hashes
    assert block_size % hash_block_size == 0
AssertionError
```

## Root cause analysis

The offload path mixes up per-group block geometry with the global hash granularity:

1. `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes()` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:~726-792`) computes for multi-group models:
   - `hash_block_size = gcd(group_block_sizes)` over **prefix-cacheable** groups — for DSV4.1-Flash: gcd(32, 8) = 8? No — in our crash the resolved `hash_block_size=32` and the group's `group_size=8`, meaning the SWA/circular-buffer group (block_size 8) was **excluded** from the hashing_sizes GCD (its `prefix_cacheable` is False for `CircularBufferSpec`/Kpool-tail style specs), so `hash_block_size` followed the full-attention group (32).
   - `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` stores this as `self.hash_block_size` and asserts `self.block_size % self.hash_block_size == 0` at init (manager.py:129) — which passes because `self.block_size` is the **scheduler** block size (LCM), not any single group's size.

2. At request time, `_select_eager_blocks_to_store()` (manager.py:720) iterates **all** KV cache groups — including the non-prefix-cacheable SWA group — and calls:
   ```python
   resolved_hashes = resolve_block_hashes(
       request.block_hashes, self.hash_block_size, group_size)
   ```
   with `group_size = 8` (the SWA group) and `hash_block_size = 32`.

3. `resolve_block_hashes()` (kv_cache_utils.py:2770-2789) only supports viewing fine hashes at a **coarser** granularity (`block_size >= hash_block_size`, enforced by the assert). Receiving `block_size(8) < hash_block_size(32)` violates its contract.

Two contributing bugs:
- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` passes a group-local block size into a function whose contract assumes the caller wants a **scheduler-level** view; for groups with `block_size < hash_block_size` the call is meaningless (there are no per-group hashes at 8-token granularity — hashes only exist at 32-token boundaries).
- The init-time assert (manager.py:129) checks the wrong invariant (`scheduler_block_size % hash_block_size == 0`), which is trivially true and hides the per-group mismatch until the first request.

## Suggested fixes

Any of these would unblock DSV4.1-Flash-class hybrid models; (1)+(2) together are probably the right combination:

1. **Skip hash resolution for non-prefix-cacheable groups** in `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` (and the lazy variant): the SWA/circular-buffer group's KV is windowed/evicted anyway, so offloading it by content hash is not meaningful. Only resolve hashes for groups whose `kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable` is True and whose `block_size >= hash_block_size`.

2. **Clamp per-group block size in the manager**: when calling `resolve_block_hashes`, pass `max(group_size, self.hash_block_size)` or round `group_size` up to a multiple of `hash_block_size`, mirroring what `BlockHashListWithBlockSize` does for the coarser direction.

3. **Harden `resolve_block_hashes`**: replace the bare assert with a descriptive error, and/or support the `block_size < hash_block_size` direction by returning the finest available view with an offset warning — though semantically this case should be prevented by the caller (fix 1).

## Extra context

- Same model + same image **without** `--kv-transfer-config` serves and benchmarks fine (stable under 100K-prefix prefix-repetition load, and single-batch decode TPS ~330-350 tok/s with DSpark), so the regression is specific to the CPU offload connector path.
- An equivalent sglang deployment with hierarchical cache (`--enable-hierarchical-cache`, host pool ~127 GB/rank paged) serves the same workload without issue, for comparison.
- We patched `kv_cache_utils.py` inside the container with a debug print before the assert to capture the failing values (`block_size=8, hash_block_size=32, modulo=8`), which is how the numbers above were obtained.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

First, a huge thank you to the entire vLLM engineering team and community. Your work on making high-performance LLM serving accessible across NVIDIA, AMD ROCm, Intel, TPU, and CPU backends is genuinely transformative — the pace of model coverage (DeepSeek V4, V4.1-Flash, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3, …), the unified frontends (Python + Rust), the disaggregation and KV-cache innovations all land in months, not years. I'm reaching out to flag a reproducible inconsistency between the official recipe documentation and what is actually published on Docker Hub, which is currently blocking a production rollout on our side.

Problem
